name: Question 2
problem:
A tank initially holds $320\,\text{L}$ of a chemical solution containing $8\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved chemical.
A chemical solution containing $0.14\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved chemical per liter is poured into the tank at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed solution leaves the tank at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min}.$ Which differential equation best describes the amount of dissolved chemical $Q,$ in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after the solution begins to be added?
worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the amount of dissolved chemical in the tank at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which dissolved chemical enters the tank minus the rate at which dissolved chemical leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{kg}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which dissolved chemical enters the tank.

First, note that a chemical solution containing $0.14\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved chemical enters the tank at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *dissolved chemical* enters the tank is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0.14\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot (18\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(0.14\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot (18\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =2.52\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which dissolved chemical exits the tank.

Now, to find the rate at which dissolved chemical leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of solution in the tank at time $t.$

- The tank initially contains $320\,\text{L}$ of solution.

- Chemical solution enters the tank at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $18t\,\text{L}$ have entered the tank.

- The completely mixed solution leaves the tank at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $18t\,\text{L}$ have left the tank.

As a result, the volume of solution in the tank after $t$ minutes is 

$$
320+18t-18t=320\,\text{L}.
$$

Since $Q$ is the mass of dissolved chemical in the tank, the *concentration* of the solution at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{320}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed solution leaves at a rate of $18\,\text{L/min},$ *dissolved chemical* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(18\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{320}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}) \\  & =(18\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{320}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}}) \\  & =\frac{18Q}{320}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{9Q}{160}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

Finally, the rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =2.52-\frac{9Q}{160}\end{aligned}
$$

which finally gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{9}{160}Q=2.52.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

A tank initially holds 320L of a chemical solution containing 8kg of dissolved chemical. A chemical solution containing 0.14kg of dissolved chemical per liter is poured into the tank at a rate of 18L/min, while the completely mixed solution leaves the tank at a rate of 18L/min. Which differential equation best describes the amount of dissolved chemical Q, in kilograms, in the tank t minutes after the solution begins to be added?

a
dQdt−9160Q=2.52
b
dQdt−120Q=2.52
c
dQdt+9160Q=0
d
dQdt+120Q=2.52
e
dQdt+9160Q=2.52
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since Q is the amount of dissolved chemical in the tank at time t, the derivative dQdt describes how this amount changes with respect to time t, in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which dissolved chemical enters the tank minus the rate at which dissolved chemical leaves the tank.

dQdt=Qin′−Qout′

Note that the units of dQdt,Qin′ and Qout′ are kg/min. Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

Step 1: Calculating the rate at which dissolved chemical enters the tank.

First, note that a chemical solution containing 0.14kg/L of dissolved chemical enters the tank at a rate of 18L/min. So, the rate at which the dissolved chemical enters the tank is

Qin′=(0.14kgL)⋅(18Lmin)=(0.14kgL)⋅(18Lmin)=2.52kgmin.

Step 2: Calculating the rate at which dissolved chemical exits the tank.

Now, to find the rate at which dissolved chemical leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of solution in the tank at time t.

  • The tank initially contains 320L of solution.

  • Chemical solution enters the tank at a rate of 18L/min. So, after t minutes, 18tL have entered the tank.

  • The completely mixed solution leaves the tank at a rate of 18L/min. So, after t minutes, 18tL have left the tank.

As a result, the volume of solution in the tank after t minutes is 320+18t−18t=320L.

Since Q is the mass of dissolved chemical in the tank, the concentration of the solution at time t is Q320kgL.

Therefore, as the completely mixed solution leaves at a rate of 18L/min, dissolved chemical leaves at a rate of Qout′=(18Lmin)⋅(Q320kgL)=(18Lmin)⋅(Q320kgL)=18Q320kgmin=9Q160kgmin.

Step 3: Calculate the overall rate of change.

Finally, the rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit:

dQdt=Qin′−Qout′=2.52−9Q160 which finally gives

dQdt+9160Q=2.52.
